name: passthrough-replicator
context: A source topic, or an external system that writes to one, must be republished to a destination topic — renamed, re-partitioned, re-keyed, filtered, or routed — with no aggregation, no windowing and no local state. The canonical topology is the Kafka Streams 'replicator': consume the input partitions as an ordinary consumer group member, optionally re-map the record, and write to an output topic whose partition count and partitioner are chosen independently of the source. Used for cross-cluster mirroring, environment-scoped topic aliasing, security re-scoping, and re-partitioning ahead of a downstream stateful sub-topology.
benefits: Stays completely stateless — no state store, no changelog, no restore step, so a restart is O(1) instead of a state replay
Decouples the destination partition count and key scheme from the source, so downstream parallelism can change without producer changes
Provides one choke point for topic-level ACLs, PII redaction and schema translation instead of N consumer-side copies of that logic
Replay and backfill reduce to re-reading an offset range from the source log; the log is the queue
Delivery semantics are an explicit choice: at-least-once by default, exactly-once when the relay commits inside a Kafka transaction
tradeoffs: Adds a full extra hop (producer to source topic, relay, destination topic) with the matching latency, cost and failure domain
Ordering is only guaranteed within a source partition; re-keying during replication breaks per-key order for every downstream stateful operator
A naive relay duplicates by default — the destination accumulates a duplicate tail unless it is compacted or the relay is transactional
Backpressure is invisible at the destination: without lag-based autoscaling an overloaded relay silently buffers instead of shedding
Cross-cluster replication is asynchronous, so there is no global ordering and cycles are possible unless provenance headers are stamped
use_cases: Mirroring a production topic into an analytics or archive cluster without exposing producers to a second cluster
Renaming topics per environment (dc1_orders to dc2_orders) so downstream clients always see a stable local name
Re-partitioning a topic to raise downstream parallelism before a stateful consumer joins it
Filtering or redacting sensitive fields once at a trusted boundary rather than in every consumer
Replaying a rebuilt destination topic from a retained source log after an accidental bad deployment
avoid_when: The relay needs to aggregate, deduplicate or join — that is a stateful topology, not a replicator
The source is a request/response API with no durable log behind it to replay from
End-to-end ordering across the whole topic is required — the topic, not the relay, is the ordering boundary
The transformation cannot be made idempotent, so replay from an arbitrary offset is unsafe
component_types: Source processor: subscribes to the input topic partitions as a normal consumer group member
Key/value re-map: optional record transformation, chosen to avoid an unnecessary repartition topic
Repartition topic: explicitly sized internal topic inserted only when the key actually changes
Sink processor: writes the destination topic with a declared partitioner and partition count
Provenance header: stamped on each replicated record to prevent a relayed record from being relayed back
anti_patterns: Re-keying without an explicit repartition topic, so downstream stateful operators silently receive data that is not co-partitioned
Mirroring inside the same cluster as if it were cross-cluster replication, doubling write load for zero isolation benefit
Relaying with at-least-once semantics into a non-compacted destination, producing an ever-growing duplicate tail
Configuring A to B and B to A relays without provenance headers, which is an infinite replication loop
Running several relays that each apply a different transformation, so the destination topic no longer has one defined meaning
design_principles: Statelessness: the relay holds no state, so recovery requires no restore step
Explicit partitioning: the destination partition count is a declared decision, never an inherited accident
Chosen delivery semantics: at-least-once or transactional exactly-once, decided rather than inherited
Unidirectional flow: replication is one-way and cycle-free by construction
Bounded blast radius: a relay failure degrades destination freshness, never the correctness of the source
best_practices: Size the destination partitions for the downstream consumer's parallelism, not for the upstream producer's convenience
Stamp provenance or origin headers so a replicated record can never be re-replicated back
Alert on consumer lag age, not record count — lag is measured in records but retention is measured in time
Keep relay logic trivial; anything with branching or aggregation belongs in a stateful topology
Make the relay idempotent so replay from an arbitrary offset is always safe
